Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No evidence of electoral register integration with government data exchange platform in CAR. Country has been through significant political instability.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original citation (harbingerstandard.com) is dead (crawl not found) and was a low-authority secondary source. Fetched World Bank Project Appraisal Document (PAD4661, March 2022) and 2023 Implementation Status Report for the CAR Public Sector Digital Governance Project (P174620): both confirm the Government "lacks a shared technical architecture and interoperability layers to facilitate the secure exchange of data between various segments of government." A May 2026 report on a new Huawei partnership confirms inter-ministerial interconnection is still at the planning/early-build stage (national data centre and microwave interconnection network not yet built). Since no cross-government data exchange exists at all, recoded from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated) — a positive finding of non-integration rather than an evidentiary gap.
revised_comments: No government-wide data exchange or interoperability platform currently operates in the Central African Republic, so the electoral register is not integrated with other government data systems. The register is compiled and maintained independently by the national electoral management body using its own data collection processes. The World Bank-financed Public Sector Digital Governance Project (2022–2026) is building early foundations, including a government data centre and a unified citizen service portal (Gouvernemental Centralisé, launched December 2025), and a 2026 partnership with Huawei aims to interconnect ministries via microwave links, but backend interoperability across government databases remains at the planning stage.

Fetched World Bank Project Appraisal Document (PAD4661, March 2022) and 2023 Implementation Status Report for the CAR Public Sector Digital Governance Project (P174620): both confirm no shared technical architecture or interoperability layer exists for exchanging data between government segments. The Dûnîa platform (launched February 2026) digitises HR, budget, and project-tracking data and adds a public statistics portal, but it is an internal system for a single ministry (Economy, Planning and International Cooperation) rather than a cross-agency data exchange linking census, civil registration, or other agencies' statistics. revised_comments: No government-wide data exchange links statistics, census, or administrative data across agencies in the Central African Republic. The Ministry of Economy, Planning and International Cooperation launched an internal digital platform (Dûnîa) in February 2026 that centralises the ministry's own budget, HR, and development-project data and includes a planned public statistics portal, but this operates within a single ministry rather than as a cross-government exchange. The World Bank-financed Public Sector Digital Governance Project (2022–2026) and a 2026 Huawei partnership to interconnect ministries and build a national data centre are laying early technical foundations, but a shared interoperability layer for planning and statistical data does not yet exist.
